question:
Which of the following pair of compound - boiling point is correct?

I. Chloroform - 334K

II. Methane - 111K
solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Chloroform **has a boiling point of **334K**. It is a **colourless, heavy, sweet-smelling, non-flammable liquid** that is used in a variety of industrial and laboratory applications.
 
• In the **human body,** it depresses the central nervous system and can cause effects ranging from **dizziness to unconsciousness. *Hence, match I is correct.***
 
• **Methane**, on the other hand, has a much lower boiling point of **111K**. Methane is a **colourless, odourless gas.**
 
• It's the main constituent of **natural gas**, which is used extensively in various industrial applications. It's also a significant greenhouse gas, with numerous environmental impacts. ***Hence, match II is also correct.***
 
• Boiling points are often used in chemistry as an indicator of the strength and types of forces among molecules in a substance. **Stronger intermolecular forces result in higher boiling points.**
